intake_scope.user_goal: Determine from current evidence how reusable LLM/AI-agent harnesses can be standardized across domains, including skill architecture, routing/composition, state, tools, security, evaluation and a proposed Harness Design Base Architecture.
in_scope: 2024-2026 primary/peer-reviewed agent research plus foundational work
out_of_scope: claiming a universal architecture is scientifically proven
vendor adoption as proof of superiority
missing_inputs: Exact deduplicated number of all search results screened is not exposed reproducibly by the web search interface; retained-source count is exact, screened-source count is NOT_REPORTED.

source_map.title: SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks
source_map.claim_supported: Curated skills can improve task success, but gains vary strongly by domain and task; self-generated skills do not help on average.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: 86 tasks, 11 domains, 7 agent-model configurations, 7,308 trajectories; curated skills +16.2 pp average; 16/84 tasks negative.

source_map.title: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Do Not
source_map.claim_supported: Skills often act as procedural anchors; large skill pools create a retrieval bottleneck.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: 8,135 trials; retrieval actual-use precision fell from 29.6% to 3.3% as pool size grew 5 to 100.

source_map.title: SWE-Skills-Bench: Do Agent Skills Actually Help in Real-World Software Engineering?
source_map.claim_supported: Skill injection is not universally useful and can add large token overhead or hurt when guidance is stale or mismatched.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: ~565 instances, 49 public skills; 39/49 zero pass-rate improvement; +1.2 pp average; up to +451% token overhead; 3 skills degraded up to -10%.

source_map.title: Generative Skill Composition for LLM Agents
source_map.claim_supported: Multi-skill composition can be modeled jointly over subset, count, and order; structured composition can outperform simple top-k retrieval.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: SkillsBench evaluation on two coding agents; +23.1 pp and +18.2 pp over no-skill; lower prompt cost than gold retrieval in reported setup.

source_map.title: Compositional Skill Routing for LLM Agents: Decompose, Retrieve, and Compose
source_map.claim_supported: Task decomposition quality is a major bottleneck for large multi-skill libraries; dependency-aware composition can reduce context use.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: 300 compositional queries, 2,209 MCP skills; standard decomposition step-level category recall 34.2%; iterative skill-aware decomposition improves reported decomposition accuracy.

source_map.title: Agent Skills Specification
source_map.claim_supported: Current Agent Skills format standardizes SKILL.md metadata and supports progressive disclosure plus optional scripts, references, and assets.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Required name and description; optional compatibility/metadata/allowed-tools; instructions and resources loaded progressively.

source_map.title: Model Context Protocol 2026-07-28 Architecture
source_map.claim_supported: MCP separates host orchestration/security from focused servers and uses explicit capability negotiation.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Client-host-server architecture; host controls permissions and lifecycle; servers expose focused resources/tools/prompts.

source_map.title: Model Context Protocol 2026-07-28 Tools and Authorization
source_map.claim_supported: Tool interfaces are schema-described and security guidance recommends user control for tool invocations; protocol state is explicit rather than implicit.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Tools have input schemas; human-in-the-loop guidance; stateful operations use explicit handles across calls.

source_map.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
source_map.claim_supported: Current engineering practice exposes distinct runtime, tool, state, orchestration, guardrail, human-review, tracing and evaluation primitives.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Official SDK documentation lists run loop/state, tools/MCP, orchestration/handoffs, guardrails/human review, tracing/evaluation as separable capabilities.

source_map.title: ToolHop: A Query-Driven Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Hop Tool Use
source_map.claim_supported: Multi-hop tool use with interdependencies remains difficult even for strong models.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: ACL 2025; 995 queries, 3,912 tools, 14 LLMs; leading reported accuracy 49.04%.

source_map.title: ToolSandbox: A Stateful, Conversational, Interactive Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Tool Use Capabilities
source_map.claim_supported: State dependencies, missing information, and dynamic tool interactions expose failures not visible in stateless one-shot benchmarks.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: NAACL Findings 2025; stateful tool execution, on-policy simulator and dynamic milestone evaluation.

source_map.title: HiAgent: Hierarchical Working Memory Management for Solving Long-Horizon Agent Tasks with Large Language Model
source_map.claim_supported: Long-horizon tasks can benefit from explicit hierarchical working-memory management.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: ACL 2025; five long-horizon tasks; reported roughly 2x success rate and 3.8 fewer average steps.

source_map.title: Memory OS of AI Agent
source_map.claim_supported: Hierarchical long-term memory can improve long-conversation retention in a memory-intensive benchmark.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: EMNLP 2025; LoCoMo, GPT-4o-mini; reported +48.36% F1 and +46.18% BLEU-1 over baselines.

source_map.title: Agent Workflow Memory
source_map.claim_supported: Reusable induced workflows can improve long-horizon web navigation and transfer across tasks/domains.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Mind2Web and WebArena, 1000+ tasks across 200+ domains; reported relative gains and cross-domain transfer.

source_map.title: StateFlow: Enhancing LLM Task-Solving through State-Driven Workflows
source_map.claim_supported: Explicit state-machine process grounding can improve success and reduce inference cost on some multi-step tool tasks.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: COLM 2024 paper; reported +13% InterCode SQL and +28% ALFWorld versus ReAct, with lower cost.

source_map.title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
source_map.claim_supported: Added autonomous-agent complexity is not always necessary for strong task performance.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Simple localization-repair-validation pipeline reported 32% SWE-bench Lite at low cost, outperforming then-current open-source agents.

source_map.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
source_map.claim_supported: Interface design between model and environment materially affects agent behavior and success.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Custom ACI evaluated on SWE-bench and HumanEvalFix; authors report substantial gains without changing model weights.

source_map.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
source_map.claim_supported: Agent reliability must be measured over repeated runs and rule-following, not only single-run task success.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Function-calling agents under 50% task success in study; pass^8 under 25% in retail for GPT-4o.

source_map.title: AgentRewardBench: Evaluating Automatic Evaluations of Web Agent Trajectories
source_map.claim_supported: Neither a single LLM judge nor rule-based evaluation is sufficient across all web-agent settings.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: 1,302 expert-reviewed trajectories, 5 benchmarks, 12 judges; no single judge best across benchmarks; rule evaluation can underreport success.

source_map.title: The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research
source_map.claim_supported: Standardized observation/action spaces and experiment management improve comparability and reproducibility of web-agent evaluation.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Unified environment evaluated six models across multiple browser benchmarks.

source_map.title: Agent Security Bench: Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
source_map.claim_supported: Agent security failures occur across prompts, tools and memory, and current defenses are incomplete.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: 10 scenarios, 400+ tools, 13 LLMs, nearly 90k cases; highest average reported ASR 84.30%.

source_map.title: LivePI: More Realistic Benchmarking of Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection
source_map.claim_supported: Indirect prompt injection remains effective in production-like tool-using agents; pre-execution authorization can sharply reduce tested harmful actions.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Seven surfaces, twelve attack families, five malicious goals; reported total ASR 10.7%-29.6%; two-layer defense intercepted tested malicious completions in one GPT-5.3-Codex setting.

source_map.title: NetInjectBench: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Large Language Model Agents for Network Operations
source_map.claim_supported: Execution-time authorization boundaries can outperform prompt-only safety in a bounded benchmark.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: 130 scenarios; naive unsafe tool action 82.5%; metadata-aware policy gate 0/240 unsafe under stated metadata-integrity assumption.

source_map.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
source_map.claim_supported: Multi-agent architectures introduce distinct specification, coordination, verification and termination failure modes; more agents do not guarantee gains.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Five/seven framework variants across 150+ tasks/traces; 14 failure modes grouped into system design, inter-agent misalignment and verification/termination.

source_map.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
source_map.claim_supported: Interleaving reasoning with environment actions is a foundational agent-loop pattern with task-specific empirical benefits.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: ICLR 2023; evaluated knowledge and interactive decision tasks.

source_map.title: Re-Invoke: Tool Invocation Rewriting for Zero-Shot Tool Retrieval
source_map.claim_supported: Tool retrieval quality is a scaling bottleneck and can be improved with retrieval-specific methods.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: EMNLP Findings 2024; +20% relative nDCG@5 single-tool and +39% multi-tool on ToolE versus reported alternatives.

source_map.title: LongFuncEval: Measuring the effectiveness of long context models for function calling
source_map.claim_supported: Large tool catalogs, long tool responses and long conversations can substantially degrade function-calling performance.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: Reported degradation ranges: 7%-85% with more tools; 7%-91% with longer tool responses; 13%-40% with longer multi-turn conversation.

source_map.title: Agent Skills in the Wild: An Empirical Study of Security Vulnerabilities at Scale
source_map.claim_supported: Skills are a supply-chain and privilege surface; executable scripts increase observed vulnerability risk.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: 42,447 skills collected, 31,132 analyzed; 26.1% with at least one vulnerability; script-bundling OR=2.12.

source_map.title: Do Not Mention This to the User: Detecting and Understanding Malicious Agent Skills in the Wild
source_map.claim_supported: Malicious skill ecosystems are an observed supply-chain threat requiring provenance, review and constrained permissions.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: USENIX Security 2026; 157 reported malicious skills removed after disclosure; paper analyzes multi-phase malicious behavior.

source_map.title: Agent Skills: A Data-Driven Analysis of Claude Skills for Extending Large Language Model Functionality
source_map.claim_supported: Public skill ecosystems are large, redundant, software-heavy and include non-trivial state-changing/system-level capabilities.
source_map.evidence_quote_or_pointer: 40,285 publicly listed skills from a major marketplace; heavy-tailed lengths and widespread intent redundancy.

tool_call.purpose: Find current primary research, counterevidence and official specifications
tool_call.inputs_summary: Independent search families for architecture, skills, routing, state/memory, evaluation, security and standardization
tool_call.expected_output: Source corpus with dated primary/official evidence

tool_call.purpose: Validate mandatory report structure and internal source references

analysis.public_reasoning_trace: Evidence was grouped by architecture mechanism rather than by vendor framework. For each proposed invariant, supporting studies were checked against counterexamples and domain limits. Architecture was synthesized only after negative evidence had ruled out a maximally agentic universal design. The report exposes decisions and evidence links, not private chain-of-thought.
counterarguments: Agentless shows that sophisticated autonomous loops can be unnecessary for some high-value tasks.
SWE-Skills-Bench shows that skills may yield almost no marginal benefit and can hurt when stale/mismatched.
Multi-agent failure research shows coordination and termination introduce new failure surfaces.
AgentRewardBench shows both deterministic and LLM-based evaluators can be wrong.
Security benchmark defenses have environment assumptions; zero observed attacks in a bounded test is not a universal guarantee.
edge_cases: Small read-only single-turn agents may collapse several planes into one implementation.
High-risk transactional agents may require stricter approval/audit layers than the base architecture.
Open-ended research agents may need flexible orchestration rather than rigid DAGs.
Large skill catalogs may need learned composition; this remains experimental in HDBA v0.1.
Persistent memory can create privacy/poisoning risks and should not be enabled merely because storage exists.

findings.claim: The evidence does not justify a single maximally agentic universal harness. A minimal kernel with complexity-gated extensions is better supported.
findings.impact: Avoids unnecessary cost, latency and coordination failure.
findings.recommendation: Default to a single-agent/direct execution path; escalate to state-machine, graph, multi-skill or multi-agent modes only when task evidence demands them.

findings.claim: Skills are useful but are not reliably beneficial merely by being present.
findings.impact: Blind skill injection can waste tokens or reduce success.
findings.recommendation: Require task-level skill evals, context compatibility, versioning and negative controls.

findings.claim: Routing/retrieval becomes a first-class subsystem as the capability catalog grows.
findings.impact: Flat exposure scales poorly and can reduce invocation precision.
findings.recommendation: Use progressive disclosure plus retriever/reranker and, for compositional tasks, dependency-aware planning.

findings.claim: Run state is core; persistent semantic/episodic memory is not.
findings.impact: Prevents overbuilding memory systems for bounded tasks.
findings.recommendation: Separate execution/artifact/checkpoint state from optional long-term memory stores.

findings.claim: Untrusted skills/retrieved content and side-effectful tools must not share the same authority as privileged harness policy.
findings.impact: Reduces prompt-injection, supply-chain and unauthorized-action risk.
findings.recommendation: Enforce instruction hierarchy, provenance, capability permissions, sandboxing, approval gates and pre-execution authorization.

findings.claim: Evaluation infrastructure is part of the harness architecture, not an afterthought.
findings.impact: Without repeated, environment-grounded evaluation, reliability claims can be false green.
findings.recommendation: Ship regression suites, repeated-run metrics, trajectory traces, deterministic validators and semantic/human review where required.

findings.claim: A Harness Preset Specification is justified as an engineering proposal, not yet as an empirically proven standard.
findings.impact: Prevents source laundering from vendor/spec adoption into scientific superiority claims.
findings.recommendation: Version HDBA v0.1, run cross-domain ablations and revise fields based on marginal value.

bias_flags: Novelty bias: 2026 Agent Skills literature is unusually preprint-heavy.
Benchmark-domain bias: many strong results come from coding, web navigation and tool-use tasks.
Vendor/specification authority bias: current standards can show interoperability practice but not superiority.
Architecture elegance bias: clean layer diagrams can overstate empirical support.
Survivorship/publication bias: positive agent interventions are more likely to be published than null deployments.
bias_and_failure_modes.overconfidence_check: Confidence is reduced where evidence is single-paper, preprint-only, domain-concentrated or lacks ablation. Exact manifest fields, universal plane boundaries and learned composition are not treated as settled science.
bias_and_failure_modes.scope_drift_check: The synthesis remains focused on repeatable harness construction and does not infer general AGI architecture claims.
bias_and_failure_modes.prompt_injection_check: Web and user-provided materials are treated as evidence/data. No retrieved instruction is permitted to override the research protocol or tool policy.

synthesis.final_answer: A standardized reusable harness is justified as an engineering reference architecture only if it is minimal, contract-driven, evaluation-bound and complexity-gated. Evidence strongly supports explicit tool/capability interfaces, run state, routing for large catalogs, validation/evaluation, and trust boundaries. Evidence does not justify mandatory persistent memory, DAGs, multi-agent decomposition, learned skill composition or a fixed ten-layer stack for every domain. HDBA v0.1 therefore defines a small invariant control kernel plus versioned domain presets and optional extensions.
synthesis.confidence_reason_public: Multiple independent peer-reviewed/primary sources support the key mechanisms and important counterexamples were found. Confidence is below 5 because the exact standardization schema and several 2026 skill-composition/security results remain preprint-heavy and lack broad replication.

human_readable_summary: The strongest evidence supports a minimal runtime kernel, explicit tool/skill contracts, scalable routing, run state, validation/evaluation and trust boundaries. The weakest parts are the exact manifest fields, universal layer boundaries, learned skill composition and universal multi-agent claims. HDBA v0.1 is therefore a falsifiable engineering reference, not a claim of settled scientific optimality.
open_questions: What is the marginal value of each HDBA plane under controlled ablation across research, coding, support, data-analysis and computer-use tasks?
At what catalog size and ambiguity level does skill retrieval outperform exposing all skill metadata for each model family?
Do skill dependency graphs transfer across model providers, or are optimal graphs harness/model specific?
Can pre-execution authorization remain effective under adversarial metadata or compromised provenance channels?
Which memory policy gives the best task-success/privacy/poisoning trade-off by task class?
How stable are skill benefits over skill/version drift and changing tools?
Can a standardized preset compiler produce behaviorally equivalent harnesses across runtimes, or only structurally equivalent ones?
Which evaluator ensembles best predict human judgments without false-green bias on long trajectories?
What complexity threshold justifies supervisor-worker or multi-agent orchestration over a single-agent/state-machine baseline?
How should learned skill composition be evaluated against simple deterministic planners under distribution shift?
